text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"just_cause_eviction","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act (good cause required for eviction or lease non-renewal)","requirement":"A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by consent or through court eviction, and must have good cause (statutory grounds) to evict or fail to renew a lease. Every cause except nonpayment of rent must be described in detail in a written notice. A Notice to Quit is required for all good-cause evictions except nonpayment of rent, and a Notice to Cease is also required for some grounds. A Judgment for Possession must be entered before the tenant must move. Self-help evictions and lockouts are illegal. Listed grounds: nonpayment of rent; disorderly conduct; property damage; substantial breach of rules or lease covenants; nonpayment of a lawful, non-unconscionable rent increase; habitual late payment; health and safety violations or removal from the market by a governmental agency; permanent retirement of the property from residential use; refusal of reasonable lease changes; condominium, cooperative or fee-simple conversion; owner or buyer occupancy for small buildings and certain condominium or cooperative units; employment-based tenancy; drug offense conviction; assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, the landlord's family or employees. The document's text is cut off partway through ground O (assault or terrorist threats), so any later grounds are not captured. Relocation assistance: a tenant evicted for illegal occupancy (G 3) is entitled to six times monthly rent, paid by the landlord. If it is not paid at least 5 days before removal, a municipal relocation fund may pay it and the landlord must repay the municipality. If there is no municipal fund, interest accrues at 18% per year and the amount is a lien on the property. Tenants evicted under ground G may be eligible for other relocation assistance, which must be provided before eviction.","key_value":"Notice to Quit periods: 3 days (disorderly conduct, property damage, employment-based tenancy, drug offense); 1 month (rule or lease breaches, rent increase nonpayment, habitual late payment, lease changes); 2 months (owner or buyer occupancy); 3 months (health and safety or removal from market); 18 months (permanent retirement from residential use); 3 years (condominium, cooperative or fee-simple conversion). Nonpayment of rent needs no Notice to Quit, but a 14-day notice is required for federally subsidized housing.
